answer: When I think back to my childhood, one face always comes to mind. I would like to talk about my best friend from childhood, who lived just a few houses down from us in Sirajganj. We met when we were barely five years old, on the very first day of primary school, and quickly became [[inseparable]]. Almost every afternoon was spent playing cricket in the lane, exploring the neighbourhood or getting into harmless mischief. During the monsoon we used to race paper boats in the flooded streets, and in the dry season we flew kites from the rooftops until our mothers called us in for dinner. Those years were wonderfully [[carefree]], with none of the responsibilities that come later. What made our friendship special was how easily we understood each other, without any of the awkwardness that adults sometimes have. As for whether we are still in touch, sadly his family moved to Rajshahi when we were teenagers, and we gradually drifted apart, which I still find a little [[melancholy]]. We do reconnect occasionally, usually by phone around Eid, and it is lovely how quickly the old bond resurfaces. The last time we met, we spent the whole evening laughing about the things we had done as boys. Honestly, childhood friendships have a special kind of [[innocence]] that is hard to recreate later in life. I look back on those days with enormous fondness, and I feel grateful to have had such a good companion growing up.

followUps.q: Would you like to spend more time with him?
followUps.answer: Definitely. I have been meaning to visit him in Rajshahi for ages, but work always gets in the way. This year I am determined to finally make the trip and spend a proper weekend together.

followUps.q: Do children today have as much freedom as you did?
followUps.answer: Probably not. Many parents worry more about safety now, and children spend more time indoors on screens. I think they miss out on the kind of outdoor adventures we [[took for granted]].

note: Added how we met (first day of primary school), monsoon paper boats and kite flying, and a clearer answer to 'still in touch' with a recent meeting.
